title: Allow rule Bash(git commit *) does not match a commit with a multi-line -m message ('*' does not cross newlines)
observed: kiln defect. Steps: approve 'git add *, git commit *, git log *' via option 2 (saved to .kiln/settings.local.json). Later Opus ran 'cd "$PWD" && git add -A && git commit -q -m "Add file-backed store...\n\ninternal/store/filestore.go: ..."' (multi-line message). kiln prompted, with no 'don't ask again' option. internal/claude/settings/settings.go MatchesRule turns '*' into '.*' and compiles '^...$' without (?s), so '.' stops at the newline inside the message. Hypothesis, not run: the same applies to deny rules, so a newline inside an argument could slip past a 'Bash(rm *)'-style deny glob.
expected: Claude Code (src/utils/permissions/shellRuleMatching.ts matchWildcardPattern) compiles with the 's' (dotAll) flag, so 'Bash(git commit *)' matches multi-line commit messages and heredocs. kiln should compile with (?s).

fix.note: e76649b on branch worktree-agent-ae1e528c60b007fe6 (not merged; unit tests only). Deny side confirmed before the fix: a Bash(rm *) deny missed rm -rf with a quoted newline (DecideIn returned allow under a Bash allow); now deny.
